elements.evidence: No exclusion language appears in the inserted Section 20.
Inserted text contains no procure/modify/replace/refund remedy; Section 9.3 still refers to 'the remedies required by Section 20.5' which do not exist.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: No cap language; 21.3 merely lists 'its indemnification obligations' as Excluded Claims.

reasons: All atomic elements of the preferred position are present in operative text: defend and indemnify Customer and Affiliates, the four triggers (IP infringement of Services/Deliverables, Vendor breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), the notice/control/cooperation procedure, and a Customer indemnity confined to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

The fallback bargain is not satisfied (no modification/combination/specification exclusions, no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, no 3× annual fees super-cap), but the levels are separate bargains and the locked preferred level is complete.

Minimal: a single concise insertion filling an entirely absent indemnification article, using existing defined terms (Affiliates, Services, Deliverables, Customer Data, Applicable Law); no hold-harmless, extra indemnitees, Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, or fallback remedies were added.

Intent preserved: Sections 9.3, 19.5 and 21.3 are untouched and remain effective. Note only that Section 9.3's pre-existing cross-reference to 'the remedies required by Section 20.5' remains unresolved because the inserted Section 20 has no remedy subsection; this dangling reference pre-dates the edit, but a short 20.5 procure/modify/replace/refund provision would cure it if desired.
